title: Polygenic-score portability: genetic-ancestry continuum as denominator-scope audit
summary: Meta-research audit record showing that denominator scope includes training-data ancestry, genetic distance, social/environmental context, and individual-level variation; it is a portability caveat for genomic evidence rather than a failure of genetics as such.

status_history.note: Added to answer rev0019 open debt about ancestry/diversity caveats.

place.scope: polygenic-score portability across genetic-ancestry continuum; no individual risk interpretation

claims.claim: Ding et al. state that polygenic scores have limited portability across groupings of individuals and, using ATLAS and UK Biobank data, show that PGS accuracy decreases individual-to-individual along the continuum of genetic ancestries.
what_would_change_status: Second-pass source review or newer primary evidence materially changes the claim scope.

claims.claim: The article warns against treating discrete ancestry clusters as sufficient: it discusses social-construct conflation, population-level accuracy metrics, unassigned individuals, and equity concerns caused by limited reference panels and aggregate metrics.
what_would_change_status: Second-pass source review or newer primary evidence materially changes the claim scope.

claims.claim: The audit record is scope-limited: the paper frames individual PGS accuracy as an upper-bound/limited construct, notes non-genetic factors and population-specific architecture issues, and emphasizes diverse training data and careful interpretation rather than declaring PGS unusable.
what_would_change_status: Second-pass source review or newer primary evidence materially changes the claim scope.

type_payload.denominator_surface: training data, target population, genetic-distance continuum, trait architecture, and social/environmental context
type_payload.numerator_surface: reported PGS accuracy or risk estimate in a target person/population
bias_mechanisms_encoded: discrete ancestry labels hide individual variation
limited reference panels leave people unclassified
limits: Does not say PGSs never work.
Does not equate genetic ancestry with race or ethnicity.

handling_notes: Do not reify race as genetics.
Use ancestry as a data/portability construct with social-context caveats.
No individual-level genetic or health data is imported.

unknowns: No systematic review of all PGS portability literature is encoded.
Clinical implementation trials and regulatory guidance not encoded.

scope_qualifiers.phenotype_scope: polygenic scores across 84 traits in cited article
scope_qualifiers.ancestry_or_population_scope: genetic ancestry continuum, ATLAS and UKBB
